blockingFindings: ISSUE: The machine register encodes gate prerequisites in a way a dispatcher cannot evaluate and that is circular for the plan's own F0a stage. MC04 `planningPrerequisites` is the aggregate `["RP01","RP03","RP02"]`, but RP02 cannot complete until F1 passes, F1 requires F0a, and F0a is MC04 component authorship (final pairing/verifier port). Read literally, MC04 F0a work can never be dispatched. Likewise MC01 lists `["RP01","RP03"]` even though MC01-ATOMIC is explicitly exempt; MC02/MC03 use the unexpanded template `RP03:{campaignId}`; package statuses (`integrated-experimental-awaiting-result-review`, `ledger-interface-source-preparation-complete`, `legacy-source-reviewed-no-current-execution-admission`) are outside the charter's allowed state set and gate statuses need a side mapping. The reconciliation itself says the dispatcher must check RP prerequisites, so this is an actionability defect, not cosmetic. FIX: define a machine-checkable prerequisite grammar (e.g. `RP02:F0:reviewed`, `RP03:campaign:<id>:admitted`, `MC01-ATOMIC:accepted`, `RP01:subset:RP01-MC03:complete`) and canonical status enums for packages, gates, stages and probes; record per-milestone prerequisites (MC01-ATOMIC, MC01-EXTENSIONS, MC04-F0a, MC04-F3, MC03-F2, MC02-I2) as separate register entries rather than package-level aggregates; remove `{campaignId}` placeholders in favour of `campaign-admission.json` record IDs resolved at admission time.

ISSUE: The F1 probe definitions do not test the interface that MC04's source record says is actually missing. The MC04 record's unresolved pieces are the 'native-0.8 verifier/transcript port into the outer circuit stack' and 'constrained final fixed-G2 pairing' inside the ledger backend, yet P1 is defined as an extraction of `test_transcript_gadget` and P3 as an extension of `test_verify_proof`, both in the native `midnight-zk` 695351f stack (proofs 0.8.0/circuits 7.1.0). A P1/P3 pass in the native stack shows native-vs-native agreement and says nothing about the outer stack selected by the ledger-family decision (ledger-8: proofs 0.7.1/circuits 6.2.0, whose four locked crate archives are not cached; ledger-9: proofs 0.8.2/circuits 7.2.4, unaligned to Preview). F1 could therefore pass with 'no waivers' while the real cross-stack boundary remains untested, and F3 would inherit an unfalsified assumption. FIX: in the F1 table and `backend-decision.json`, require the F0 ledger-family decision to name the exact outer circuit stack (crate versions, lock hashes, feature set, SRS) in which P1 and P3 are compiled; define the native stack as reference oracle only; state that if the outer stack's exact sources are unavailable, P1/P3 are `incomplete-with-named-missing-input` (source acquisition) and F3 is blocked; if P1/P3 are retained as F2 gates, state that F2 is blocked too, or re-scope per the non-blocking finding on F2 gating.

ISSUE: The plan's stop behaviour at F0/F1 no-go is not actionable. It says no-go 'permits bounded work on the missing Midnight boundary' and that product-scope change needs a new user instruction, but it enumerates no candidate alternative routes, owners, resource envelopes or an escalation trigger. Given that F0a asks MC04 to author an absent constrained BLS final-pairing finalizer (Fq12/Miller loop) under a k<=17 ceiling that already exhausted a far smaller loan relation, a finalizer no-go is a realistic outcome; under the current text it would stall F1->F2->F3 with only the instruction 'work on that boundary'. FIX: add to F0 an explicit route-alternatives disposition list with one row per candidate (constrained finalizer in the chosen outer stack; ledger-9 V3 alignment with deployment-provenance evidence; any ledger-native accumulator/deferred-pairing support discovered at newer pins; deterministic-only or host-boolean routes marked FORBIDDEN), each with owner, source-inspection task, resource decision and go/no-go criterion; define the condition under which all routes are exhausted and a user escalation is recorded instead of further spending; state which evidence (e.g. P2 export/import) may still be gathered independently of the finalizer decision.
nonblockingFindings: F2 (fixed-instance native loan IVC) is gated on P3 (constrained pairing), which is an MC04/F3 concern; the native verifier already performs the host final check, so F2's genuine prerequisites are P2 (export/import needed for retained-byte verification), F0 route closure and RP01-MC03. Either justify why P3 must precede F2 or gate F2 on F0+P1+P2 and F3 on P3; otherwise a finalizer no-go also blocks cheap, independent native feasibility evidence.

Resource headroom is asserted but not evidenced: the register sums to exactly 850 minutes/33 dispatches (60+385+35+85+50+50+50+110+25), the plan says MC01-ATOMIC uses its 'already delegated' allocation and RP01 reviews use the planning-audit bank, yet no remaining-balance figures for MC01 (385 reserved) or planning audits (60 reserved) appear. Record spent/remaining per reservation in the register before any MC01-ATOMIC or RP01 review dispatch; the packet gives no basis to conclude these fit.

Charter drift: MORIARTY-COMPLETION-PROGRAM.md still states 'S2, specified-only', a 480-minute/24-dispatch reservation table and MC01 at 50 min/4 dispatches, while the register is 'executing' at 850/33 with MC01 at 385/13. The charter marks the envelope 'historical' but the table is presented as current. Mark the table superseded with a pointer to the register amendments, and align allowed package states with the register's strings.

F0a asks for 'implemented-source reviews' of Rust that has never been compiled (compilation deferred to F1 admission). Reviewing uncompiled circuit code is weak evidence; consider admitting a bounded, non-proving `cargo check`/type-check step under the F0a preparation allocation so reviewers see a compiling candidate.

Preview deployment provenance (node binary/backend/SRS/feature set) is a stated F0 requirement but has no owner, task, or admission for its acquisition, and the fixture note forbids network access for generators. Add an explicit read-only provenance-acquisition task (owner MC04) with its own bounded admission; without it the ledger-family decision can only ever be 'explicitly unverified assumption'.

P2 (PoseidonChain<1>, two transitions) is admitted at 'k at most 17'; the original R3 loan relation exhausted rows at k17. Require a recorded constraint estimate for the recursive wrapper before admitting the generator, and state that a k17 exhaustion here is a stop, not a reason to raise k.
The paragraph assigning the twelve candidate holdouts to MC07 task R.1 appears under RP02 but belongs to RP01; move it to avoid ownership confusion in the gate records.

ROADMAP mermaid omits direct dependencies MC01->MC04, MC01->MC07 and ADM->MC05..MC08 that the register carries; the text says the register is authoritative, but add a one-line note under the diagram or include the edges to avoid a misleading critical-path reading.

Gate-record schema (`schemaVersion`, `inputs/outputs` hashes, review receipts) is described in prose only; publish the JSON schema for `semantic-challenges.json`, `backend-decision.json` and `campaign-admission.json` before the first write so reviewers can validate rather than infer.

Citations checked against supplied excerpts (DeFi 664, 824-928, 1140; PCD 679-683, 859-905, 1115; intents 1922-1954, 2014-2016, 2192-2194) are accurate. Intents 2498-2509 and several other cited ranges are outside the packet and were not verified.

The MC01 'input-boundary correction' (decodeEvaluation per the PCD review) has no acceptance test stated in any supplied document; MC01-ATOMIC acceptance should name the failing-then-passing test and bind it to the successor hash.
acceptedScope: Plan review only of openspec/REPORT-RECONCILIATION-2026-09-07.md and ROADMAP.md against the register, charter, MC04 source record, fixture note and three report reviews. Accepted as correct in the candidate: (1) Midnight-centric product target with NEAR/EVM/Cardano as comparative-only, no adapter deliverables; (2) rejection of DeFi report line 664 unbounded domains in favour of finite registered bounds and total decidable evaluation; (3) rejection of optional/deferred PCD (intents 2014-2016, PCD 1115, DeFi 1140) with mandatory four-claim acceptance and no fallback removing a mandatory claim; (4) retention of private witness handoff and genuine split/branch/join proofs in MC06 despite intents 1922-1954; (5) preservation of all 277 ACTUS fixtures, 32 taxonomy dispositions and 72 DeFi rows with 349 explicitly not a coverage denominator; (6) honest framing of existing evidence — MC01 experimental atomic subset not accepted, fixed native candidate unrun, R3 k17 exhaustion retained as failure, no complete native-to-Preview wrapper at inspected pins, hello-world receipt insufficient; (7) the eight DeFi regression classes, eight intent cases, five composition operators and theorem ledger as RP01 design-map obligations; (8) exact-output vs minimum-receive and attenuation-as-subset clarifications; (9) forbidding host verification booleans and nonrecursive re-proof substitution; (10) separation of MC01-ATOMIC from MC01-EXTENSIONS so I2/F2 do not wait on full RP01. No implementation, proof, execution result, deployment fact or resource sufficiency is approved.
limits: Offline audit with no filesystem, git, network or execution access; all judgments rest on the embedded packet text. Line-number citations were verified only where the packet supplied the corresponding excerpt. The three report reviews, MC04 source record and fixture note are secondary extractions whose underlying source facts (crate versions, cache contents, function line numbers, absence of a constrained pairing implementation) were not independently confirmed. No Preview deployment facts, node versions or SRS provenance are established. Register arithmetic (850 minutes, 33 dispatches) was recomputed from the supplied JSON; spent balances, evidence files, MC01 tasks/spec, package READMEs and prior audit receipts were not supplied and were not assumed. No other reviewer's verdict was available or used; process status fields were not treated as evidence.
